entry.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
entry.summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

entry.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
entry.summary: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

entry.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
entry.summary: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

entry.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
entry.summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

entry.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
entry.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

entry.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
entry.summary: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

entry.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
entry.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

entry.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
entry.summary: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
